section_desc: This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. It extends to the whole of India. It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint. This Act replaces the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (Act 45 of 1860). All references to IPC in any other law shall be construed as references to this Act.

In this Sanhita, unless the context otherwise requires: 'child' means any person below the age of eighteen years; 'document' means any matter expressed or described upon any substance by means of letters, figures or marks; 'electronic record' shall have the meaning assigned to it in the Information Technology Act, 2000; 'gender' — the pronoun 'he' and its derivatives are used of any person whether male, female or transgender; 'Government' denotes the Central Government or the Government of a State; 'injury' denotes any harm whatever illegally caused to any person in body, mind, reputation or property; 'public servant' has the same meaning as assigned in section 2(4) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.

The punishments to which offenders are liable under the provisions of this Sanhita are: death; imprisonment for life; imprisonment which is of two descriptions namely rigorous and simple; forfeiture of property; fine; community service. Community service is a new punishment added which was not present in the IPC — it involves unpaid work for the benefit of the community.

A man is said to commit rape if he penetrates his penis to any extent into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a woman; or inserts any object or part of body not being penis into vagina, urethra or anus of a woman; or manipulates any part of body of a woman to cause penetration; or applies his mouth to vagina, anus, urethra of a woman, under circumstances falling under seven descriptions including against her will, without her consent, with consent obtained by fear, and when she is under eighteen years of age. Corresponds to Section 375 IPC.

Whoever, except in the cases provided for in sub-section (2), commits rape, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life. Sub-section (2) prescribes enhanced punishment (not less than ten years, extending to life) for rape by police officer, public servant, armed forces personnel, on women in custody, during communal violence, on pregnant woman, on woman under 16 years. Corresponds to Section 376 IPC.

section_title: Punishment for rape in certain cases
section_desc: Whoever commits rape on a woman under twelve years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, and shall also be liable to fine or with death. Whoever commits rape on a woman under sixteen years shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment not less than twenty years.

Where a woman is raped by one or more persons constituting a group or acting in furtherance of a common intention, each of those persons shall be deemed to have committed the offence of rape and shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, and with fine. Corresponds to Section 376D IPC.

section_title: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
section_desc: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine. Corresponds to Section 354 IPC.

Any man who watches, or captures the image of a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually have the expectation of not being observed either by the perpetrator or by any other person at the behest of the perpetrator or disseminates such image shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year, but which may extend to three years. Corresponds to Section 354C IPC.

section_title: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty
section_desc: Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. 'Cruelty' means wilful conduct likely to drive woman to suicide or cause grave injury, or harassment for dowry. Corresponds to Section 498A IPC.

Except in the cases hereinafter excepted, culpable homicide is murder if the act by which the death is caused is done with the intention of causing death; or if it is done with the intention of causing such bodily injury as the offender knows to be likely to cause the death of the person to whom the harm is caused; or if it is done with the intention of causing bodily injury to any person and the bodily injury intended to be inflicted is sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death. Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. Corresponds to Sections 299-302 IPC.

Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. When a group of five or more persons commits murder on grounds of race, caste or community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief or any other similar ground, each member of such group shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than seven years and shall also be liable to fine. This adds a new provision for mob lynching. Corresponds to Section 302 IPC with new mob lynching provision.

section_title: Culpable homicide by causing death of person other than person whose death was intended
section_desc: If a person, by doing anything which he intends or knows to be likely to cause death, commits culpable homicide by causing the death of any person, whose death he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause, the culpable homicide committed by the offender is of the description of which it would have been if he had caused the death of the person whose death he intended. Corresponds to Section 301 IPC — transferred malice doctrine.

Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and, if hurt is caused to any person by such act, the offender shall be liable either to imprisonment for life, or to such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned. Corresponds to Section 307 IPC.

Whoever commits organised crime shall be punished: if such offence has resulted in the death of any person, with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine not less than ten lakh rupees; in any other case, with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than five years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. 'Organised crime' means any continuing unlawful activity including kidnapping, robbery, extortion, land grabbing, financial scams, cyber crimes, human trafficking by a member of a organised crime syndicate. This is a NEW section not present in IPC.

Whoever does any act with intent to threaten or likely to threaten the unity, integrity, security, economic security or sovereignty of India or with intent to strike terror or likely to strike terror in the people or any section of the people in India or in any foreign country by using bombs, dynamite, firearms, poisonous gases, biological, radioactive or nuclear substances, or by any other means to cause death, injuries, damage to property, disruption of essential services, commits a terrorist act. Punishment: death or life imprisonment if death results; 5 years to life otherwise. NEW provision directly in BNS (previously only in UAPA).

section_title: Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
section_desc: Whoever, purposely or knowingly, by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or by electronic communication or by use of financial means, or otherwise, excites or attempts to excite, secession or armed rebellion or subversive activities, or encourages feelings of separatist activities or endangers sovereignty or unity and integrity of India; or indulges in or commits any such act shall be punished with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. This replaces Section 124A IPC (Sedition) which was frequently misused.

Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft. Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. Corresponds to Sections 378-379 IPC.

Whoever intentionally puts any person in fear of any injury to that person, or to any other, and thereby dishonestly induces the person so put in fear to deliver to any person any property, or valuable security or anything signed or sealed which may be converted into a valuable security, commits extortion. Punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. Corresponds to Sections 383-384 IPC.

Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, commits criminal breach of trust. Punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. Corresponds to Sections 405-406 IPC.

Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, or intentionally induces the person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he were not so deceived, and which act or omission causes or is likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind, reputation or property, is said to cheat. Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property shall be punished with imprisonment up to seven years and fine. Corresponds to Sections 415-420 IPC.

Whoever makes any false document or false electronic record or part of a document or electronic record with intent to cause damage or injury, to the public or to any person, or to support any claim or title, or to cause any person to part with property, or to enter into any express or implied contract, or with intent to commit fraud or that fraud may be committed, commits forgery. Punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Corresponds to Sections 463-465 IPC.

Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause alarm to that person, or to cause that person to do any act which he is not legally bound to do, or to omit to do any act which that person is legally entitled to do, as the means of avoiding the execution of such threat, commits criminal intimidation. Punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Corresponds to Sections 503-506 IPC.

Whoever by words either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or by visible representations, makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm, or knowing or having reason to believe that such imputation will harm, the reputation of such person, is said to defame that person. Punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Corresponds to Sections 499-500 IPC. Note: Now also covers online/digital defamation explicitly.

This Sanhita may be called the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. It extends to the whole of India. This Act replaces the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC). All references to CrPC in any other law shall be construed as references to this Sanhita. The BNSS contains 531 sections and introduces digital/electronic provisions for trials and investigations.

In this Sanhita: 'audio-video electronic means' means use of any communication device for the purposes of video conferencing, recording of processes of identification, search and seizure, or evidence; 'bail' means release from custody on furnishing surety; 'complaint' means any allegation made orally or in writing to a Magistrate; 'investigation' includes all proceedings under this Sanhita for collection of evidence; 'Magistrate' means a Metropolitan Magistrate, Judicial Magistrate or Executive Magistrate; 'police report' means a report forwarded by an officer in charge of a police station to a Magistrate.

section_title: Arrest of persons — when police may arrest without warrant
section_desc: Any police officer may without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant, arrest any person who has been concerned in any cognizable offence or against whom a reasonable complaint has been made; who is in possession of any implement of house-breaking; who is a proclaimed offender; in whose possession anything is found which may reasonably be suspected to be stolen property. No person accused of an offence punishable for less than seven years imprisonment shall be arrested by the police officer unless there are reasons to be recorded in writing. Corresponds to Section 41 CrPC with enhanced safeguards.

Every arrested person shall have: the right to have a person of his choice informed of the arrest; the right to have the grounds of arrest communicated to him in a language he understands; the right to consult a legal practitioner of his choice; the right to be examined by a medical officer if so requested; the right to inform a nominated person through police of his arrest. NEW provision: The arrested person must be informed of his rights immediately upon arrest. Any violation shall be an offence by the police officer.

section_title: Attachment of property of persons absconding
section_desc: If any person against whom a warrant has been issued by a Court has absconded or is concealing himself so that the warrant cannot be executed, the Court may publish a written proclamation requiring such person to appear at a specified place and at a specified time not less than thirty days from the date of publishing. The Court may also issue a simultaneous order for attachment of property. Corresponds to Section 83 CrPC.

Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, if given orally to an officer in charge of a police station, shall be reduced to writing by him or under his direction, and be read over to the informant. Every such information shall be signed by the person giving it. The substance thereof shall be entered in a book to be kept by such officer. A copy of FIR shall be provided to the informant free of charge. NEW: The FIR can now be filed electronically and the officer must register the FIR within three days. Corresponds to Section 154 CrPC with electronic FIR provision.

NEW provision: An officer in charge of a police station shall ensure that a forensic expert visits the crime scene for all offences punishable with imprisonment of seven years or more. The forensic expert shall collect evidence and prepare a report. Such forensic evidence shall be digitally recorded. If no forensic expert is available, the officer shall document reasons in writing. This provision makes forensic investigation mandatory for serious offences.

section_title: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in twenty-four hours
section_desc: Whenever any person is arrested and detained in custody and it appears the investigation cannot be completed within twenty-four hours, the officer in charge shall transmit a copy of entries in the diary and shall produce the accused before a Magistrate. The Magistrate may authorise detention of the accused in such custody as such Magistrate thinks fit, for a term not exceeding fifteen days at a time, but no Magistrate shall authorise detention of the accused person in custody for a total period exceeding ninety days if the offence is punishable with death, imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term not less than ten years, and sixty days in other cases. BNSS adds: State may extend to 180 days in terrorist/organised crime cases. Corresponds to Section 167 CrPC.

section_title: Conditions for bail in case of non-bailable offences
section_desc: When any person accused of, or suspected of, the commission of any non-bailable offence is arrested or detained without warrant by an officer in charge of a police station or appears or is brought before a Court, he may be released on bail, but no such person shall be so released if there appear reasonable grounds for believing that he has been guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life; or if the offence is a cognizable offence and he had been previously convicted of an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life or imprisonment for seven years or more. Bail in special cases: when accused is a sick or infirm person, a person below 18 years of age, or a woman except in offences punishable with death. Corresponds to Section 437 CrPC.

NEW provision in BNSS: All trials, inquiries and proceedings may be conducted by use of electronic video linkage or audio-video electronic means, with the consent of the parties, or as directed by the court. The recording of such proceedings shall have the same evidentiary value as if conducted in person. This provision modernises criminal trials by allowing virtual hearings. Evidence may be recorded through video conferencing. Witness examination through electronic means is now explicitly permitted.

Any investigation, inquiry or trial pending at the commencement of this Sanhita shall continue to be governed by the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, until its completion, unless directed otherwise by the Court. All appeals and revisions pending before courts at the commencement of this Sanhita shall be disposed of under CrPC. All fresh cases filed after the commencement date shall be governed by BNSS.

This Act may be called the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023. It extends to the whole of India. This Act replaces the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. All references to the Indian Evidence Act in any other law shall be construed as references to this Act. The BSA contains 170 sections and includes updated provisions for electronic and digital evidence.

In this Act: 'document' means any matter expressed or described upon any substance by means of letters, figures or marks, or by more than one of those means, and includes any electronic or digital record; 'evidence' means and includes all statements which the Court permits or requires to be made before it by witnesses in relation to matters of fact under inquiry; all documents including electronic or digital records produced for the inspection of the Court; 'electronic record' has the meaning assigned under the Information Technology Act; 'digital signature' means authentication by electronic means as defined under IT Act.

No confession made to a police officer shall be proved as against a person accused of any offence. This provision maintains the bar from Section 25 IEA to prevent police torture and coerced confessions. The absolute bar on admissibility of confession to police officer is retained. Only confessions leading to discovery of facts (Section 23) remain admissible to that extent. Corresponds to Section 25 IEA.

section_title: Relevancy of judgments of Courts of Justice
section_desc: Judgments of Courts of Justice are relevant facts in the following cases: a final judgment, order or decree which by law prevents any Court from taking cognizance of a suit or holding a trial, is relevant whether such judgment, order or decree is or is not pleadable as res judicata. The judgment of a Court of Justice shall be taken into consideration as a relevant fact to determine the issues between the same parties. Corresponds to Sections 40-44 IEA.

Primary evidence means the document itself produced for the inspection of the Court. Secondary evidence means certified copies; copies made from the original by mechanical processes; copies made from or compared with the original; counterparts of documents; and oral accounts of the contents of a document given by some person who has himself seen it. Electronic records and digital documents are now expressly included in primary evidence when authentic certificates are provided. Corresponds to Sections 62-63 IEA with digital expansion.

Any information contained in an electronic record which is printed on paper, stored, recorded or copied in optical or magnetic media produced by a computer or a communication device shall be deemed to be a document and shall be admissible in proceedings without further proof of production of the original, if the conditions relating to its authenticity are satisfied as per the certificate requirements. The certificate must be signed by the person responsible for operating or managing the computer system. An electronic record is now on par with written documents. Corresponds to Section 65B IEA with simplified certification process.

The burden of proof in a suit or proceeding lies on that person who would fail if no evidence at all were given on either side. The burden of proof as to any particular fact lies on that person who wishes the Court to believe in its existence. In criminal cases, the prosecution bears the burden to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt. In civil cases, the standard is preponderance of probabilities. Corresponds to Sections 101-103 IEA.

When one person has, by his declaration, act or omission, intentionally caused or permitted another person to believe a thing to be true and to act upon such belief, neither he nor his representative shall be allowed, in any suit or proceeding between himself and such person or his representative, to deny the truth of that thing. Types: estoppel by record, by deed, by conduct. Corresponds to Section 115 IEA.

Any question suggesting the answer which the person putting it wishes or expects to receive is called a leading question. Leading questions must not, if objected to by the adverse party, be asked in an examination-in-chief, or in a re-examination, except with the permission of the Court. Leading questions may be asked in cross-examination. Corresponds to Sections 141-143 IEA.

The credit of a witness may be impeached in the following ways by the adverse party, or, with the consent of the Court, by the party who calls him: by the evidence of persons who testify that they, from their knowledge of the witness, believe him to be unworthy of credit; by proof that the witness has been bribed, or has accepted the offer of a bribe, or has received any other corrupt inducement to give his evidence; by proof of former statements inconsistent with any part of his evidence which is liable to be contradicted. Corresponds to Section 155 IEA.

In this Act: 'consent manager' means a person registered with the Board, who acts as a single point of contact to enable a Data Principal to give, manage, review and withdraw her consent through an accessible, transparent and interoperable platform; 'data' means a representation of information, facts, concepts, opinions or instructions in a manner suitable for communication, interpretation or processing by human beings or by automated means; 'data fiduciary' means any person who alone or in conjunction with other persons determines the purpose and means of processing of personal data; 'data principal' means the individual to whom the personal data relates and where such individual is a child includes the parents or lawful guardian; 'personal data' means any data about an individual who is identifiable by or in relation to such data.

A Data Fiduciary may process the personal data of a Data Principal only in accordance with the provisions of this Act for a lawful purpose for which the Data Principal has given her consent; or for certain legitimate uses. Legitimate uses include: for the State and its instrumentalities for performing any function under law or in the interest of sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the State; for compliance with any judgment or order issued under any law; for responding to a medical emergency; for employment purposes.

Before seeking the consent of the Data Principal, or at the time of seeking consent if such data was collected before the commencement of this Act, the Data Fiduciary shall give to the Data Principal a notice informing her of: the personal data and the purpose for which it is proposed to be processed; the manner in which she may exercise her rights under this Act; the manner in which she may make a complaint to the Board; the details of the Consent Manager, where applicable.

Consent given by the Data Principal shall be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous with a clear affirmative action, and shall signify an agreement to the processing of her personal data for the specified purpose and be limited to such personal data as is necessary for such specified purpose. The Data Principal shall have the right to withdraw consent at any time, with the ease of withdrawing consent being comparable to the ease with which consent was given. Upon withdrawal, the Data Fiduciary shall cease processing the personal data within a reasonable time.

A Data Principal shall have the right to: obtain information about personal data processed, and a summary of the processing activities undertaken by the Data Fiduciary; in case the personal data has been shared by the Data Fiduciary with other Data Fiduciaries, identities of all such Data Fiduciaries with whom the personal data has been shared; correction of inaccurate or misleading personal data; completion of incomplete personal data; updating of personal data; erasure of personal data that is no longer necessary for the purpose for which it was processed.
chapter_title: Rights and Duties of Data Principals

section_desc: The Central Government may, by notification, exempt from the application of any or all provisions of this Act, any Data Fiduciary or class of Data Fiduciaries: in the interest of sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States or maintenance of public order; for the purpose of preventing, detecting, investigating or prosecuting any offence or contravention of any law; for research, archiving or statistical purposes.

The Board may, after inquiry, impose penalty on a Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager for non-compliance: failure to take security safeguards — penalty up to Rs 250 crore; failure to notify Data Principal or Board in case of personal data breach — penalty up to Rs 200 crore; non-fulfilment of obligations under special provisions for processing children's data — penalty up to Rs 200 crore; breach of voluntary undertaking — penalty up to Rs 10,000 crore; other non-compliance — penalty up to Rs 50 crore.

In this Act: 'assigned spectrum' means spectrum assigned under Section 4; 'authorisation' means an authorisation granted under Section 3; 'interconnection' means physical or logical linking of telecommunication networks; 'message' means any sign, signal, writing, image, sound, data or intelligence of any nature transmitted, emitted or received over a telecommunication network; 'telecommunication' means transmission, emission or reception of messages through wire, radio, optical, or other electromagnetic systems; 'telecommunication network' means the system of telecommunication equipment or infrastructure.

The Central Government may, by auction or by administrative process, assign spectrum to authorised entities for provision of telecommunication services. Spectrum shall not be assigned without following the due process and conditions prescribed. Spectrum assigned to Defence and other notified government entities shall be exempt from auction. The assignment shall be made for a period not exceeding twenty years and may be renewed. Spectrum assigned shall not be transferred without prior approval of the Central Government.

The Central Government or a State Government may, if satisfied that it is necessary or expedient so to do in the interest of sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States, or public order, or for preventing incitement to the commission of any cognizable offence, by order, direct any authorised entity to intercept or monitor messages or class of messages. Such interception must follow prescribed safeguards and the order must be reviewed by a review committee.

act: Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2021
section_title: Grant of mining lease by competitive bidding for certain mineral blocks
section_desc: The State Government shall, by notification, specify the mineral blocks for which mining lease shall be granted by competitive bidding through auction. The State Government shall fix the floor price for the mineral block to be auctioned. The successful bidder shall be granted a mining lease for a period not exceeding fifty years. The amendment of 2021 allows private sector participation in commercial mining of coal without restriction on end use.

The Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 decriminalises 183 provisions across 42 Acts by converting imprisonment to fines or administrative penalties. Key amendments include: removal of imprisonment provisions from Indian Post Office Act, Public Liability Insurance Act, Drugs and Cosmetics Act (minor violations), Chartered Accountants Act, Industries Development Act, and various other Acts. The objective is to ease of doing business and reduce unnecessary criminalization of business activities.

'Human rights' means the rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity of the individual guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in the International Covenants and enforceable by courts in India; 'National Human Rights Commission' means the Commission constituted under section 3; 'State Human Rights Commission' means the Commission constituted under section 21; 'violation of human rights' means violation of any right guaranteed under the Constitution or the International Covenants.

The Commission shall perform all or any of the following functions: inquire, on its own initiative or on a petition presented to it by a victim or any person on his behalf, into complaint of violation of human rights; intervene in any proceeding involving any allegation of violation of human rights pending before a court; review the safeguards provided by or under the Constitution or any law for the protection of human rights; study treaties and other international instruments on human rights and make recommendations.
